touches.text: artifact: the one door a record of truth changes through, and the journal of who came through it (hash-chained, caller read from the kernel). WHY: errors are permanent in records of truth (Law 7), and the journal is what shows a record moved by hand. USERS: everyone who writes a record. [Q#91: The caller class is read from the kernel's cgroup path, so on Windows it reads null and the class comes only from env vars (CAIRN_USER, CLAUDECODE, CAIRN_OPERATOR); gate cannot be reached, and 3 teeth in test_artifact_door.py say UNRAN. Measured 2026-11-12: the Windows parent process chain does show claude.exe above a shell. Is Windows a first-class caller platform (an exe-name chain: claude.exe is cc, a console with no claude above it is akien, a service session is gate), or env-fallback only?]
Coding Ticket: what we usually mean.
Inference Ticket: the record of one call to the inference proxy, everything that happened to that request.
Trouble Ticket: an error that needs a non-automated fixer (CC or Akien).
Shareable provenance (charters, tickets, validations) is git JSON beside the code, never a row.

Seals: one current validation per proof, beside the proof. A seal holds while the code it measured is unchanged. [Q#90: A proof's seal is one record, so the newest OS to seal replaces the other's, and a proof with teeth for both OSes reds on every single OS. Measured 2026-11-12: a Windows reseal of a mixed proof overwrote the Linux seal. Do seals go per OS (validations/<os>/, or an OS key in the record), or is one OS the sealing box?]
Test runs are transient (30 days, 4.3.2); seals are records of truth (git).

CC's memory lives in a private git repo of its own, linked into the place Claude Code looks for it on each box, so every CC instance is the same CC whichever box it runs on. Its distillations (the method, and CC's patterns to avoid) are published in the CC device in cairn; how we got there, and anything of CC's history of Akien, stays in the private repo. WHY: cairn and CairnCommons are public. "How Akien does it" is meant for anybody; Akien himself, and the people around him, are not. A memory starts private; only a distillation crosses, and Akien reviews what crosses.
